definition.def: When a child or young animal matures, it becomes an adult.
examples: You will learn what to expect as your child matures physically. [VERB]
The eggs hatched and the chicks matured. [VERB]

definition.def: When something matures, it reaches a state of complete development.
examples: When the trees matured they were cut in certain areas. [VERB]

definition.def: If someone matures, they become more fully developed in their personality and emotional behaviour.
examples: Hopefully after three years at university I will have matured. [VERB]
I thought you had matured enough not to be giggly and silly about serious art. [VERB]

definition.def: If you describe someone as mature, you think that they are fully developed and balanced in their personality and emotional behaviour. [approval]
examples: They are emotionally mature and should behave responsibly.
You and I are mature, freethinking adults.

definition.def: If you describe the work of an artist, writer, or musician as mature, you mean that it is thoughtful and skilful and shows that their abilities have fully developed. [approval]
examples: It is his most mature comedy yet.

definition.def: If something such as wine or cheese matures or is matured, it is left for a time to allow its full flavour or strength to develop.
examples: Unlike wine, brandy matures only in wood, not glass. [VERB]
...the cellars where the cheeses are matured. [be VERB-ed]

definition.def: Mature cheese or wine has been left for a time to allow its full flavour or strength to develop.
examples: ...the best place to enjoy fine, mature wines.

definition.def: When an investment such as a savings policy or pension plan matures, it reaches the stage when you stop paying money and the company pays you back the money you have saved, and the interest your money has earned. [business]
examples: These bonuses will be paid when your savings plan matures in ten years' time. [VERB]
...an endowment policy that matured on September 1. [VERB]

definition.def: If you say that someone is mature or of mature years, you are saying politely that they are middle-aged or old. [politeness]

examples.sentence: Geschwind and Galaburda knew that different parts of the brain mature at different rates; the right hemisphere develops first, then the left.
A Shelterwood Cut, which only takes place in a mature forest that has already been thinned several times, involves removing all the mature trees when other seedlings have become established.
The most serious is increasing mortality, especially of mature trees.
Together these eight companies operated as a mature oligopoly, essentially running the entire market.
She's quite mature for her age and she can already write her name and read a little.
Mature breeding birds are very expensive, even a fertilized ostrich egg isn't cheap.
This is very different from the situation in the wild, where the vast majority of chicks will die or be killed before they grow up into mature ostriches.
I suppose it's the same for all mature students?
Firstly, we'll plant mature pine trees to provide shelter and shade just to the right of the supermarket in Days Road.
Well, the first thing is I'd prefer a hall where there are other mature students, if possible.
